removed: {{fa}}Have you graduated beyond the clip-on tie? Beginning with these helpful instructions, a sharp-looking tie, a mirror, and some patience, you can become an expert in tying your own fashionable knot. You have several options available, from the versatile Four-in-Hand Knot to the classic Windsor.
If you're helping someone else put on a tie, [[Tie-a-Tie-on-Someone-Else|see this article]] for instructions from that perspective.

#Drape the tie around your neck. With your collar up and your shirt fully buttoned, place the tie around your shoulders. Hang the wider end of the tie on your right side, with the narrow end about 12 inches (30 cm) higher on the left.<ref>https://www.thetiebar.com/how-to-tie/four-in-hand</ref>[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 1 Version 14.jpg|center]]
#*Avoid spread collars with this small, asymmetric knot.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Bring the wide end to the left side of your body, over the narrow end. Hold the two pieces of cloth together with your left hand, near your neck.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 12.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 2-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 12.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 12.360p.first.gif}}

#Loop the wide end under the narrow end. Let go with your right hand. Tuck it underneath the narrow end, grab the wide end, and pull it back through to your right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Loop the wide end under the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 12.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 3-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 12.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 12.360p.first.gif}}

#Loop the wide end back over again. Cross it over the narrow end one more time, at the same point where your left hand is holding the knot together. The front of the tie should be facing forward again (so the seam is hidden).{{Imagecaptionbottom |

Loop the wide end back over again}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 4-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end up through the neck loop. Fold the tip of the wide end under itself and pull up through the neck loop.https://www.thetiebar.com/how-to-tie/four-in-hand{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 5-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Insert the wide end down through the front knot. You should have a horizontal knot across the front of your tie. Hold this knot open with your finger and carefully insert the wide end.{{Imagecaptionbottom |

Insert the wide end down through the front knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 6-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Tighten the knot. Hold the narrow end and slide the front knot up to tighten the tie. Make sure your tie is straight and the length is appropriate, ideally ending at the top of your belt buckle.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Tighten the knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 7-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Place the tie upside down around your collar. Unlike most knots, the Pratt knot begins with the tie upside down, so the seam of the tie is facing forward. Hang the wide end of the tie over your right side, and the narrow end over your left side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Place the tie upside down around your collar}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 11.jpg|center]]
#*This medium size knot suits most collars and builds.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>

#Check the position of the wide end. In a knotted tie, the wide end should just graze the top of your belt buckle.<ref>http://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052702303491404579391701064546672</ref> At the start, however, raise or lower the wide end until it hangs 1–2 inches (2.5–5 cm) below this point. As a rule of thumb, the Pratt knot will lift the wide end by this distance as you tie the knot.<ref>http://www.realmenrealstyle.com/pratt-shelby-milanese-necktie-knot/</ref>{{Imagecaptiontop | Check the position of the wide end}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 11.jpg|center]]

#*The narrow end of the tie should be higher than the wide end. It will usually be around belly button level, but this is less important than the wide end's placement.<ref>http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/pratt</ref>

#Cross the wide end under the narrow end. Move the wide end across your body to the left side, placing it underneath the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end under the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 10-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#*Do not move the narrow end of the tie for any part of this knot.<ref>http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/pratt</ref> Just hold it steady while you use the wide end.

#Bring the wide end up to the loop around the neck. Place the tip on top of the loop, still on your left side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring the wide end up to the loop around the neck}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 11-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

Pull the wide end through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 12-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end over the narrow end, from left to right. This flips the wide end so the seam is no longer visible. The wide end will extend at an angle off to your right.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end over the narrow end, from left to righ}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 13-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end up through the neck loop. Bring the wide end up to your neck loop again, but this time from below. Pull it through.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 14-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Tuck the wide end down through the new loop at the front. Your last fold created a horizontal loop at the front of your tie. Tuck the wide end through this loop, and pull straight down to tighten. The wide end should now rest in front of the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Tuck the wide end down through the new loop at the front}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 15-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Slide the knot to adjust. Pull down on the wide end to tighten. Slide the front knot up to the base of your collar to fasten the tie.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Slide the knot to adjust}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 16-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#*To create a dimple just below the front knot, squeeze the sides of the knot gently as you tighten.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/pratt/</ref>

#Position the wide end on the right side. Place the tie around your neck and let the sides hang in front of you. The wide end should be on the right side of your body, and hang roughly 12 inches (30 cm) lower than the narrow end on the left.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/halfwindsor/</ref>{{Imagecaptiontop |
Position the wide end on the right side}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 10.jpg|center]]

#*The Half Windsor is a triangular, symmetrical knot suitable for formal occasions. Larger than the Four-in-hand but less bulky than the Windsor, this can work with most neckties and collar types.<ref>Chic Simple, ''Shirt and Tie'', p. 37, (1993), ISBN 0-500-01593-7</ref> Neckties made from thicker fabric will likely require a spread or wide spread collar with this knot.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Bring the wide end of the tie over to your left side, crossing over the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 18-preview Version 8.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end back under the narrow end. Complete a loop around the narrow end and pull the wide end back to the right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end back under the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 19-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Take the wide end up to the neck loop. Raise the wide end up to the loop of necktie at your collar. Keep it on the right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Take the wide end up to the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 20-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end through the loop and to the left. Insert the wide tip down through the loop and pull it through from the left side, so it crosses under the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end through the loop and to the left}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 21-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end over the front of the narrow end. Bring the wide end back across the front and onto your right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end over the front of the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 22-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Slide the wide end up through the neck loop. Fold the wide end up through the neck loop a second time.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Slide the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 23-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Insert the wide end down through the front knot. Loosen the front knot with your finger and insert the wide end. Pull it through to rest over the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Insert the wide end down through the front knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 24-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull on the wide end to tighten. Gently squeeze the front knot as you pull to slide the knot up and create a dimple at the front of your tie.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull on the wide end to tighten}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 25-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Put the tie around your neck. Make sure the wider end is on the right, and about 14 inches (36 cm) lower than the thinner side on the left.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/windsor/</ref> The Windsor knot uses a lot of cloth, so the lower end should start a bit lower than you would usually position a tie.{{Imagecaptiontop | Put the tie around your neck}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 10.jpg|center]]

#*Many consider the large, symmetric Windsor knot the most elegant and formal option. Wear it with a spread or wide spread collar.<ref>Thuy Tranthi, ''Tie a Windsor Knot'', in ''The Expert's Guide to 100 Things Everyone Should Know How to Do'', p. 51, (2004), ISBN 1-74114-586-4</ref>

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Hold one end in each hand, then pass each of them to the opposite hand. The wide end should now be on your left side.http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/windsorhttp://www.tie-a-tie.net/windsor/{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 28-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold it end behind the narrow end. Grab the wide end with your right hand and pull it back to the right side of your body, under the narrow end. Hold the knot near your collar in place with your left hand.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold it end behind the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 30-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end up to the neck loop from the front. Keep it on the right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring the wide end up to the neck loop from the front}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 31-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 32-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end over the narrow end. Fold it back over from right to left, so the front side is visible again.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end over the narrow end}}

added: ===Using the Easiest Method (Four-in-Hand Knot)===

#Drape the tie around your neck. With your collar up and your shirt fully buttoned, place the tie around your shoulders. Hang the wider end of the tie on your right side, with the narrow end about 12 inches (30 cm) higher on the left.<ref>https://www.thetiebar.com/how-to-tie/four-in-hand</ref>[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 1 Version 14.jpg|center]]
#*Avoid spread collars with this small, asymmetric knot.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Bring the wide end to the left side of your body, over the narrow end. Hold the two pieces of cloth together with your left hand, near your neck.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 12.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 2-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 12.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 12.360p.first.gif}}

#Loop the wide end under the narrow end. Let go with your right hand. Tuck it underneath the narrow end, grab the wide end, and pull it back through to your right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Loop the wide end under the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 12.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 3-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 12.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 12.360p.first.gif}}

#Loop the wide end back over again. Cross it over the narrow end one more time, at the same point where your left hand is holding the knot together. The front of the tie should be facing forward again (so the seam is hidden).{{Imagecaptionbottom |

Loop the wide end back over again}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 4-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end up through the neck loop. Fold the tip of the wide end under itself and pull up through the neck loop.https://www.thetiebar.com/how-to-tie/four-in-hand{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 5-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Insert the wide end down through the front knot. You should have a horizontal knot across the front of your tie. Hold this knot open with your finger and carefully insert the wide end.{{Imagecaptionbottom |

Insert the wide end down through the front knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 6-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Tighten the knot. Hold the narrow end and slide the front knot up to tighten the tie. Make sure your tie is straight and the length is appropriate, ideally ending at the top of your belt buckle.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Tighten the knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 7-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#*Squeeze the sides of the knot gently to create a dimple just below it.
#*The four-in-hand knot is a little asymmetrical at the neck. Don't worry about this; it is normal.
===Tying the Pratt Knot (Basic Formal Knot)===

#Place the tie upside down around your collar. Unlike most knots, the Pratt knot begins with the tie upside down, so the seam of the tie is facing forward. Hang the wide end of the tie over your right side, and the narrow end over your left side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Place the tie upside down around your collar}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 11.jpg|center]]
#*This medium size knot suits most collars and builds.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>

#Check the position of the wide end. In a knotted tie, the wide end should just graze the top of your belt buckle.<ref>http://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052702303491404579391701064546672</ref> At the start, however, raise or lower the wide end until it hangs 1–2 inches (2.5–5 cm) below this point. As a rule of thumb, the Pratt knot will lift the wide end by this distance as you tie the knot.<ref>http://www.realmenrealstyle.com/pratt-shelby-milanese-necktie-knot/</ref>{{Imagecaptiontop | Check the position of the wide end}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 11.jpg|center]]

#*The narrow end of the tie should be higher than the wide end. It will usually be around belly button level, but this is less important than the wide end's placement.<ref>http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/pratt</ref>

#Cross the wide end under the narrow end. Move the wide end across your body to the left side, placing it underneath the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end under the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 10-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#*Do not move the narrow end of the tie for any part of this knot.<ref>http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/pratt</ref> Just hold it steady while you use the wide end.

#Bring the wide end up to the loop around the neck. Place the tip on top of the loop, still on your left side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring the wide end up to the loop around the neck}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 11-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#Pull the wide end through the neck loop. Insert the wide end down into the loop from above. Pull it through in the same direction it lay before, on the left.{{Imagecaptionbottom |

Pull the wide end through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 12-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end over the narrow end, from left to right. This flips the wide end so the seam is no longer visible. The wide end will extend at an angle off to your right.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end over the narrow end, from left to righ}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 13-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end up through the neck loop. Bring the wide end up to your neck loop again, but this time from below. Pull it through.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 14-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Tuck the wide end down through the new loop at the front. Your last fold created a horizontal loop at the front of your tie. Tuck the wide end through this loop, and pull straight down to tighten. The wide end should now rest in front of the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Tuck the wide end down through the new loop at the front}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 15-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Slide the knot to adjust. Pull down on the wide end to tighten. Slide the front knot up to the base of your collar to fasten the tie.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Slide the knot to adjust}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 16-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#*To create a dimple just below the front knot, squeeze the sides of the knot gently as you tighten.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/pratt/</ref>
=== Tying a Half Windsor Knot (Formal)===

#Position the wide end on the right side. Place the tie around your neck and let the sides hang in front of you. The wide end should be on the right side of your body, and hang roughly 12 inches (30 cm) lower than the narrow end on the left.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/halfwindsor/</ref>{{Imagecaptiontop |
Position the wide end on the right side}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 10.jpg|center]]

#*The Half Windsor is a triangular, symmetrical knot suitable for formal occasions. Larger than the Four-in-hand but less bulky than the Windsor, this can work with most neckties and collar types.<ref>Chic Simple, ''Shirt and Tie'', p. 37, (1993), ISBN 0-500-01593-7</ref> Neckties made from thicker fabric will likely require a spread or wide spread collar with this knot.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Bring the wide end of the tie over to your left side, crossing over the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 18-preview Version 8.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end back under the narrow end. Complete a loop around the narrow end and pull the wide end back to the right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end back under the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 19-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}
#*The underside of the wide end should be visible at this point.

#Take the wide end up to the neck loop. Raise the wide end up to the loop of necktie at your collar. Keep it on the right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Take the wide end up to the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 20-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end through the loop and to the left. Insert the wide tip down through the loop and pull it through from the left side, so it crosses under the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end through the loop and to the left}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 21-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end over the front of the narrow end. Bring the wide end back across the front and onto your right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end over the front of the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 22-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Slide the wide end up through the neck loop. Fold the wide end up through the neck loop a second time.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Slide the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 23-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Insert the wide end down through the front knot. Loosen the front knot with your finger and insert the wide end. Pull it through to rest over the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Insert the wide end down through the front knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 24-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull on the wide end to tighten. Gently squeeze the front knot as you pull to slide the knot up and create a dimple at the front of your tie.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull on the wide end to tighten}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 25-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}
=== Tying the Traditional Windsor Knot (Extra Formal)===

#Put the tie around your neck. Make sure the wider end is on the right, and about 14 inches (36 cm) lower than the thinner side on the left.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/windsor/</ref> The Windsor knot uses a lot of cloth, so the lower end should start a bit lower than you would usually position a tie.{{Imagecaptiontop | Put the tie around your neck}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 10.jpg|center]]

#*Many consider the large, symmetric Windsor knot the most elegant and formal option. Wear it with a spread or wide spread collar.<ref>Thuy Tranthi, ''Tie a Windsor Knot'', in ''The Expert's Guide to 100 Things Everyone Should Know How to Do'', p. 51, (2004), ISBN 1-74114-586-4</ref>

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Hold one end in each hand, then pass each of them to the opposite hand. The wide end should now be on your left side.http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/windsorhttp://www.tie-a-tie.net/windsor/{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 27-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end up through the neck loop. Using your right hand, hold the two ends where they cross near your collar. With your left hand, pull the wide end up through the neck loop from below.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 28-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring your tie back down. Rest the wide end back on your chest, to the left of the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring your tie back down}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 29-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold it end behind the narrow end. Grab the wide end with your right hand and pull it back to the right side of your body, under the narrow end. Hold the knot near your collar in place with your left hand.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold it end behind the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 30-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end up to the neck loop from the front. Keep it on the right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring the wide end up to the neck loop from the front}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 31-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end through the neck loop. Insert the tip of the wide end and pull through, still on the right side. The underside of the wide end should now be facing forward.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 32-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end over the narrow end. Fold it back over from right to left, so the front side is visible again.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 33-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end through the neck loop from below. Bring the wide end back up through the neck loop one last time.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end through the neck loop from below}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 34-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Insert the wide end through the front knot. Place the wide end through the horizontal knot at the front of the tie. Pull it through.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Insert the wide end through the front knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 35-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 11.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Tighten the knot. Hold the base of the front knot and squeeze gently from the sides. Slowly pull the wide end of the tie to bring the knot closer to the neck.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Tighten the knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 36-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 16-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#*To create a dimple just below the front knot, squeeze the sides of the knot gently as you tighten.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/pratt/</ref>
=== Tying a Half Windsor Knot (Formal)===

#Position the wide end on the right side. Place the tie around your neck and let the sides hang in front of you. The wide end should be on the right side of your body, and hang roughly 12 inches (30 cm) lower than the narrow end on the left.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/halfwindsor/</ref>{{Imagecaptiontop |
Position the wide end on the right side}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 10.jpg|center]]

#*The Half Windsor is a triangular, symmetrical knot suitable for formal occasions. Larger than the Four-in-hand but less bulky than the Windsor, this can work with most neckties and collar types.<ref>Chic Simple, ''Shirt and Tie'', p. 37, (1993), ISBN 0-500-01593-7</ref> Neckties made from thicker fabric will likely require a spread or wide spread collar with this knot.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Bring the wide end of the tie over to your left side, crossing over the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 18-preview Version 8.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end back under the narrow end. Complete a loop around the narrow end and pull the wide end back to the right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end back under the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 19-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}
#*The underside of the wide end should be visible at this point.

#Take the wide end up to the neck loop. Raise the wide end up to the loop of necktie at your collar. Keep it on the right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Take the wide end up to the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 20-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end through the loop and to the left. Insert the wide tip down through the loop and pull it through from the left side, so it crosses under the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end through the loop and to the left}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 21-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end over the front of the narrow end. Bring the wide end back across the front and onto your right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end over the front of the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 22-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Slide the wide end up through the neck loop. Fold the wide end up through the neck loop a second time.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Slide the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 23-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Insert the wide end down through the front knot. Loosen the front knot with your finger and insert the wide end. Pull it through to rest over the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Insert the wide end down through the front knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 24-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull on the wide end to tighten. Gently squeeze the front knot as you pull to slide the knot up and create a dimple at the front of your tie.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull on the wide end to tighten}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 25-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}
=== Tying the Traditional Windsor Knot (Extra Formal)===

#Put the tie around your neck. Make sure the wider end is on the right, and about 14 inches (36 cm) lower than the thinner side on the left.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/windsor/</ref> The Windsor knot uses a lot of cloth, so the lower end should start a bit lower than you would usually position a tie.{{Imagecaptiontop | Put the tie around your neck}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 10.jpg|center]]

#*Many consider the large, symmetric Windsor knot the most elegant and formal option. Wear it with a spread or wide spread collar.<ref>Thuy Tranthi, ''Tie a Windsor Knot'', in ''The Expert's Guide to 100 Things Everyone Should Know How to Do'', p. 51, (2004), ISBN 1-74114-586-4</ref>

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Hold one end in each hand, then pass each of them to the opposite hand. The wide end should now be on your left side.http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/windsorhttp://www.tie-a-tie.net/windsor/{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 27-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end up through the neck loop. Using your right hand, hold the two ends where they cross near your collar. With your left hand, pull the wide end up through the neck loop from below.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 28-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring your tie back down. Rest the wide end back on your chest, to the left of the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring your tie back down}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 29-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold it end behind the narrow end. Grab the wide end with your right hand and pull it back to the right side of your body, under the narrow end. Hold the knot near your collar in place with your left hand.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold it end behind the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 30-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end up to the neck loop from the front. Keep it on the right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring the wide end up to the neck loop from the front}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 31-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end through the neck loop. Insert the tip of the wide end and pull through, still on the right side. The underside of the wide end should now be facing forward.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 32-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end over the narrow end. Fold it back over from right to left, so the front side is visible again.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 33-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end through the neck loop from below. Bring the wide end back up through the neck loop one last time.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end through the neck loop from below}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 34-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Insert the wide end through the front knot. Place the wide end through the horizontal knot at the front of the tie. Pull it through.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Insert the wide end through the front knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 35-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 11.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Tighten the knot. Hold the base of the front knot and squeeze gently from the sides. Slowly pull the wide end of the tie to bring the knot closer to the neck.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Tighten the knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 36-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

added: ===Using the Easiest Method (Four-in-Hand Knot)===

#Drape the tie around your neck. With your collar up and your shirt fully buttoned, place the tie around your shoulders. Hang the wider end of the tie on your right side, with the narrow end about 12 inches (30 cm) higher on the left.<ref>https://www.thetiebar.com/how-to-tie/four-in-hand</ref>[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 1 Version 14.jpg|center]]
#*Avoid spread collars with this small, asymmetric knot.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Bring the wide end to the left side of your body, over the narrow end. Hold the two pieces of cloth together with your left hand, near your neck.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 12.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 2-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 12.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 12.360p.first.gif}}

#Loop the wide end under the narrow end. Let go with your right hand. Tuck it underneath the narrow end, grab the wide end, and pull it back through to your right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Loop the wide end under the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 12.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 3-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 12.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 12.360p.first.gif}}

#Loop the wide end back over again. Cross it over the narrow end one more time, at the same point where your left hand is holding the knot together. The front of the tie should be facing forward again (so the seam is hidden).{{Imagecaptionbottom |

Loop the wide end back over again}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 4-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end up through the neck loop. Fold the tip of the wide end under itself and pull up through the neck loop.https://www.thetiebar.com/how-to-tie/four-in-hand{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 5-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Insert the wide end down through the front knot. You should have a horizontal knot across the front of your tie. Hold this knot open with your finger and carefully insert the wide end.{{Imagecaptionbottom |

Insert the wide end down through the front knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 6-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Tighten the knot. Hold the narrow end and slide the front knot up to tighten the tie. Make sure your tie is straight and the length is appropriate, ideally ending at the top of your belt buckle.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Tighten the knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 7-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#*Squeeze the sides of the knot gently to create a dimple just below it.
#*The four-in-hand knot is a little asymmetrical at the neck. Don't worry about this; it is normal.
===Tying the Pratt Knot (Basic Formal Knot)===

#Place the tie upside down around your collar. Unlike most knots, the Pratt knot begins with the tie upside down, so the seam of the tie is facing forward. Hang the wide end of the tie over your right side, and the narrow end over your left side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Place the tie upside down around your collar}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 11.jpg|center]]
#*This medium size knot suits most collars and builds.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>

#Check the position of the wide end. In a knotted tie, the wide end should just graze the top of your belt buckle.<ref>http://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052702303491404579391701064546672</ref> At the start, however, raise or lower the wide end until it hangs 1–2 inches (2.5–5 cm) below this point. As a rule of thumb, the Pratt knot will lift the wide end by this distance as you tie the knot.<ref>http://www.realmenrealstyle.com/pratt-shelby-milanese-necktie-knot/</ref>{{Imagecaptiontop | Check the position of the wide end}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 11.jpg|center]]

#*The narrow end of the tie should be higher than the wide end. It will usually be around belly button level, but this is less important than the wide end's placement.<ref>http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/pratt</ref>

#Cross the wide end under the narrow end. Move the wide end across your body to the left side, placing it underneath the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end under the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 10-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#*Do not move the narrow end of the tie for any part of this knot.<ref>http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/pratt</ref> Just hold it steady while you use the wide end.

#Bring the wide end up to the loop around the neck. Place the tip on top of the loop, still on your left side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring the wide end up to the loop around the neck}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 11-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#Pull the wide end through the neck loop. Insert the wide end down into the loop from above. Pull it through in the same direction it lay before, on the left.{{Imagecaptionbottom |

Pull the wide end through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 12-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end over the narrow end, from left to right. This flips the wide end so the seam is no longer visible. The wide end will extend at an angle off to your right.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end over the narrow end, from left to righ}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 13-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end up through the neck loop. Bring the wide end up to your neck loop again, but this time from below. Pull it through.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 14-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Tuck the wide end down through the new loop at the front. Your last fold created a horizontal loop at the front of your tie. Tuck the wide end through this loop, and pull straight down to tighten. The wide end should now rest in front of the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Tuck the wide end down through the new loop at the front}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 15-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Slide the knot to adjust. Pull down on the wide end to tighten. Slide the front knot up to the base of your collar to fasten the tie.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Slide the knot to adjust}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 16-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring your tie back down. Rest the wide end back on your chest, to the left of the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring your tie back down}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 29-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold it end behind the narrow end. Grab the wide end with your right hand and pull it back to the right side of your body, under the narrow end. Hold the knot near your collar in place with your left hand.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold it end behind the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 30-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end up to the neck loop from the front. Keep it on the right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring the wide end up to the neck loop from the front}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 31-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end through the neck loop. Insert the tip of the wide end and pull through, still on the right side. The underside of the wide end should now be facing forward.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 32-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end over the narrow end. Fold it back over from right to left, so the front side is visible again.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 33-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end through the neck loop from below. Bring the wide end back up through the neck loop one last time.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end through the neck loop from below}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 34-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Insert the wide end through the front knot. Place the wide end through the horizontal knot at the front of the tie. Pull it through.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Insert the wide end through the front knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 35-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 11.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Tighten the knot. Hold the base of the front knot and squeeze gently from the sides. Slowly pull the wide end of the tie to bring the knot closer to the neck.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Tighten the knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 36-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

removed: ===Using the Easiest Method (Four-in-Hand Knot)===

#Drape the tie around your neck. With your collar up and your shirt fully buttoned, place the tie around your shoulders. Hang the wider end of the tie on your right side, with the narrow end about 12 inches (30 cm) higher on the left.<ref>https://www.thetiebar.com/how-to-tie/four-in-hand</ref>[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 1 Version 14.jpg|center]]
#*Avoid spread collars with this small, asymmetric knot.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Bring the wide end to the left side of your body, over the narrow end. Hold the two pieces of cloth together with your left hand, near your neck.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 12.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 2-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 12.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 12.360p.first.gif}}

#Loop the wide end under the narrow end. Let go with your right hand. Tuck it underneath the narrow end, grab the wide end, and pull it back through to your right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Loop the wide end under the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 12.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 3-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 12.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 12.360p.first.gif}}

#Loop the wide end back over again. Cross it over the narrow end one more time, at the same point where your left hand is holding the knot together. The front of the tie should be facing forward again (so the seam is hidden).{{Imagecaptionbottom |

Loop the wide end back over again}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 4-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end up through the neck loop. Fold the tip of the wide end under itself and pull up through the neck loop.https://www.thetiebar.com/how-to-tie/four-in-hand{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 5-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Insert the wide end down through the front knot. You should have a horizontal knot across the front of your tie. Hold this knot open with your finger and carefully insert the wide end.{{Imagecaptionbottom |

Insert the wide end down through the front knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 6-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Tighten the knot. Hold the narrow end and slide the front knot up to tighten the tie. Make sure your tie is straight and the length is appropriate, ideally ending at the top of your belt buckle.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Tighten the knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 7-preview Version 11.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 14.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#*Squeeze the sides of the knot gently to create a dimple just below it.
#*The four-in-hand knot is a little asymmetrical at the neck. Don't worry about this; it is normal.
===Tying the Pratt Knot (Basic Formal Knot)===

#Place the tie upside down around your collar. Unlike most knots, the Pratt knot begins with the tie upside down, so the seam of the tie is facing forward. Hang the wide end of the tie over your right side, and the narrow end over your left side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Place the tie upside down around your collar}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 11.jpg|center]]
#*This medium size knot suits most collars and builds.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>

#Check the position of the wide end. In a knotted tie, the wide end should just graze the top of your belt buckle.<ref>http://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052702303491404579391701064546672</ref> At the start, however, raise or lower the wide end until it hangs 1–2 inches (2.5–5 cm) below this point. As a rule of thumb, the Pratt knot will lift the wide end by this distance as you tie the knot.<ref>http://www.realmenrealstyle.com/pratt-shelby-milanese-necktie-knot/</ref>{{Imagecaptiontop | Check the position of the wide end}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 11.jpg|center]]

#*The narrow end of the tie should be higher than the wide end. It will usually be around belly button level, but this is less important than the wide end's placement.<ref>http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/pratt</ref>

#Cross the wide end under the narrow end. Move the wide end across your body to the left side, placing it underneath the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end under the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 10-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#*Do not move the narrow end of the tie for any part of this knot.<ref>http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/pratt</ref> Just hold it steady while you use the wide end.

#Bring the wide end up to the loop around the neck. Place the tip on top of the loop, still on your left side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring the wide end up to the loop around the neck}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 11-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#Pull the wide end through the neck loop. Insert the wide end down into the loop from above. Pull it through in the same direction it lay before, on the left.{{Imagecaptionbottom |

Pull the wide end through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 12-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end over the narrow end, from left to right. This flips the wide end so the seam is no longer visible. The wide end will extend at an angle off to your right.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end over the narrow end, from left to righ}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 13-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end up through the neck loop. Bring the wide end up to your neck loop again, but this time from below. Pull it through.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 14-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Tuck the wide end down through the new loop at the front. Your last fold created a horizontal loop at the front of your tie. Tuck the wide end through this loop, and pull straight down to tighten. The wide end should now rest in front of the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Tuck the wide end down through the new loop at the front}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 15-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Slide the knot to adjust. Pull down on the wide end to tighten. Slide the front knot up to the base of your collar to fasten the tie.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Slide the knot to adjust}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 16-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#*To create a dimple just below the front knot, squeeze the sides of the knot gently as you tighten.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/pratt/</ref>
=== Tying a Half Windsor Knot (Formal)===

#Position the wide end on the right side. Place the tie around your neck and let the sides hang in front of you. The wide end should be on the right side of your body, and hang roughly 12 inches (30 cm) lower than the narrow end on the left.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/halfwindsor/</ref>{{Imagecaptiontop |
Position the wide end on the right side}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 10.jpg|center]]

#*The Half Windsor is a triangular, symmetrical knot suitable for formal occasions. Larger than the Four-in-hand but less bulky than the Windsor, this can work with most neckties and collar types.<ref>Chic Simple, ''Shirt and Tie'', p. 37, (1993), ISBN 0-500-01593-7</ref> Neckties made from thicker fabric will likely require a spread or wide spread collar with this knot.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Bring the wide end of the tie over to your left side, crossing over the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 18-preview Version 8.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end back under the narrow end. Complete a loop around the narrow end and pull the wide end back to the right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end back under the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 19-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}
#*The underside of the wide end should be visible at this point.

#Take the wide end up to the neck loop. Raise the wide end up to the loop of necktie at your collar. Keep it on the right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Take the wide end up to the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 20-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end through the loop and to the left. Insert the wide tip down through the loop and pull it through from the left side, so it crosses under the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end through the loop and to the left}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 21-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end over the front of the narrow end. Bring the wide end back across the front and onto your right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end over the front of the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 22-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Slide the wide end up through the neck loop. Fold the wide end up through the neck loop a second time.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Slide the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 23-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Insert the wide end down through the front knot. Loosen the front knot with your finger and insert the wide end. Pull it through to rest over the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Insert the wide end down through the front knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 24-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull on the wide end to tighten. Gently squeeze the front knot as you pull to slide the knot up and create a dimple at the front of your tie.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull on the wide end to tighten}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 25-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}
=== Tying the Traditional Windsor Knot (Extra Formal)===

#Put the tie around your neck. Make sure the wider end is on the right, and about 14 inches (36 cm) lower than the thinner side on the left.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/windsor/</ref> The Windsor knot uses a lot of cloth, so the lower end should start a bit lower than you would usually position a tie.{{Imagecaptiontop | Put the tie around your neck}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 10.jpg|center]]

#*Many consider the large, symmetric Windsor knot the most elegant and formal option. Wear it with a spread or wide spread collar.<ref>Thuy Tranthi, ''Tie a Windsor Knot'', in ''The Expert's Guide to 100 Things Everyone Should Know How to Do'', p. 51, (2004), ISBN 1-74114-586-4</ref>

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Hold one end in each hand, then pass each of them to the opposite hand. The wide end should now be on your left side.http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/windsorhttp://www.tie-a-tie.net/windsor/{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 27-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end up through the neck loop. Using your right hand, hold the two ends where they cross near your collar. With your left hand, pull the wide end up through the neck loop from below.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 28-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring your tie back down. Rest the wide end back on your chest, to the left of the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring your tie back down}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 29-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold it end behind the narrow end. Grab the wide end with your right hand and pull it back to the right side of your body, under the narrow end. Hold the knot near your collar in place with your left hand.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold it end behind the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 30-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end up to the neck loop from the front. Keep it on the right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring the wide end up to the neck loop from the front}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 31-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end through the neck loop. Insert the tip of the wide end and pull through, still on the right side. The underside of the wide end should now be facing forward.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 32-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end over the narrow end. Fold it back over from right to left, so the front side is visible again.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 33-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end through the neck loop from below. Bring the wide end back up through the neck loop one last time.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end through the neck loop from below}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 34-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Insert the wide end through the front knot. Place the wide end through the horizontal knot at the front of the tie. Pull it through.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Insert the wide end through the front knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 35-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 11.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Tighten the knot. Hold the base of the front knot and squeeze gently from the sides. Slowly pull the wide end of the tie to bring the knot closer to the neck.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Tighten the knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 36-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

As a rule of thumb, the Pratt knot will lift the wide end by this distance as you tie the knot.<ref>http://www.realmenrealstyle.com/pratt-shelby-milanese-necktie-knot/</ref>{{Imagecaptiontop | Check the position of the wide end}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 11.jpg|center]]

#*The narrow end of the tie should be higher than the wide end. It will usually be around belly button level, but this is less important than the wide end's placement.<ref>http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/pratt</ref>

#Cross the wide end under the narrow end. Move the wide end across your body to the left side, placing it underneath the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end under the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 10-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#*Do not move the narrow end of the tie for any part of this knot.<ref>http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/pratt</ref> Just hold it steady while you use the wide end.

#Bring the wide end up to the loop around the neck. Place the tip on top of the loop, still on your left side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Bring the wide end up to the loop around the neck}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 11-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#Pull the wide end through the neck loop. Insert the wide end down into the loop from above. Pull it through in the same direction it lay before, on the left.{{Imagecaptionbottom |

Pull the wide end through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 12-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end over the narrow end, from left to right. This flips the wide end so the seam is no longer visible. The wide end will extend at an angle off to your right.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end over the narrow end, from left to righ}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 13-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end up through the neck loop. Bring the wide end up to your neck loop again, but this time from below. Pull it through.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 14-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Tuck the wide end down through the new loop at the front. Your last fold created a horizontal loop at the front of your tie. Tuck the wide end through this loop, and pull straight down to tighten. The wide end should now rest in front of the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Tuck the wide end down through the new loop at the front}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 15-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}

#Slide the knot to adjust. Pull down on the wide end to tighten. Slide the front knot up to the base of your collar to fasten the tie.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Slide the knot to adjust}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 16-preview Version 10.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 11.360p.first.gif}}
#*To create a dimple just below the front knot, squeeze the sides of the knot gently as you tighten.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/pratt/</ref>
=== Tying a Half Windsor Knot (Formal)===

#Position the wide end on the right side. Place the tie around your neck and let the sides hang in front of you. The wide end should be on the right side of your body, and hang roughly 12 inches (30 cm) lower than the narrow end on the left.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/halfwindsor/</ref>{{Imagecaptiontop |
Position the wide end on the right side}}[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 10.jpg|center]]

#*The Half Windsor is a triangular, symmetrical knot suitable for formal occasions. Larger than the Four-in-hand but less bulky than the Windsor, this can work with most neckties and collar types.<ref>Chic Simple, ''Shirt and Tie'', p. 37, (1993), ISBN 0-500-01593-7</ref> Neckties made from thicker fabric will likely require a spread or wide spread collar with this knot.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Bring the wide end of the tie over to your left side, crossing over the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Cross the wide end over the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 9.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 18-preview Version 8.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 9.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 9.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end back under the narrow end. Complete a loop around the narrow end and pull the wide end back to the right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end back under the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 19-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}
#*The underside of the wide end should be visible at this point.

#Take the wide end up to the neck loop. Raise the wide end up to the loop of necktie at your collar. Keep it on the right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Take the wide end up to the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 20-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end through the loop and to the left. Insert the wide tip down through the loop and pull it through from the left side, so it crosses under the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull the wide end through the loop and to the left}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 21-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end over the front of the narrow end. Bring the wide end back across the front and onto your right side.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Fold the wide end over the front of the narrow end}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 22-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Slide the wide end up through the neck loop. Fold the wide end up through the neck loop a second time.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Slide the wide end up through the neck loop}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 23-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Insert the wide end down through the front knot. Loosen the front knot with your finger and insert the wide end. Pull it through to rest over the narrow end.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Insert the wide end down through the front knot}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 24-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull on the wide end to tighten. Gently squeeze the front knot as you pull to slide the knot up and create a dimple at the front of your tie.{{Imagecaptionbottom | Pull on the wide end to tighten}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 25-preview Version 9.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 10.360p.first.gif}}
=== Tying the Traditional Windsor Knot (Extra Formal)===

#Put the tie around your neck.
