removed: {{fa}}Have you graduated beyond the clip-on tie? Beginning with these helpful instructions, a sharp-looking tie, a mirror, and some patience, you can become an expert in tying your own fashionable knot. You have several options available, from the versatile Four-in-Hand Knot to the classic Windsor.
If you're helping someone else put on a tie, [[Tie-a-Tie-on-Someone-Else|see this article]] for instructions from that perspective.
[[Category:Ties]]
[[Category:Knot Tying]]
==Steps==
===Four-in-Hand Knot (Easiest Method)===

#Drape the tie around your neck. With your collar up and your shirt fully buttoned, place the tie around your shoulders. Hang the wider end of the tie on your right side, with the narrow end about 12 inches (30 cm) higher on the left.<ref>https://www.thetiebar.com/how-to-tie/four-in-hand</ref>[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 1 Version 11.jpg|center]]
#*Avoid spread collars with this small, asymmetric knot.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Bring the wide end to the left side of your body, over the narrow end. Hold the two pieces of cloth together with your left hand, near your neck.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 11.jpg|center]]

#Loop the wide end under the narrow end. Let go with your right hand. Tuck it underneath the narrow end, grab the wide end, and pull it back through to your right side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 11.jpg|center]]

#Loop the wide end back over again. Cross it over the narrow end one more time, at the same point where your left hand is holding the knot together. The front of the tie should be facing forward again (so the seam is hidden).[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 11.jpg|center]]

#Pull the wide end up through the neck loop. Fold the tip of the wide end under itself and pull up through the neck loop.<ref>https://www.thetiebar.com/how-to-tie/four-in-hand</ref>[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 11.jpg|center]]

#Insert the wide end down through the front knot. You should have a horizontal knot across the front of your tie. Hold this knot open with your finger and carefully insert the wide end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 11.jpg|center]]

#Tighten the knot. Hold the narrow end and slide the front knot up to tighten the tie. Make sure your tie is straight and the length is appropriate, ideally ending at the top of your belt buckle.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 11.jpg|center]]
#*Squeeze the sides of the knot gently to create a dimple just below it.
#*The four-in-hand knot is a little asymmetrical at the neck. Don't worry about this; it is normal.
===Pratt Knot (Basic Formal Knot)===

#Place the tie upside down around your collar. Unlike most knots, the Pratt knot begins with the tie upside down, so the seam of the tie is facing forward. Hang the wide end of the tie over your right side, and the narrow end over your left side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 8.jpg|center]]
#*This medium size knot suits most collars and builds.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>

#Check the position of the wide end. In a knotted tie, the wide end should just graze the top of your belt buckle.<ref>http://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052702303491404579391701064546672</ref> At the start, however, raise or lower the wide end until it hangs 1–2 inches (2.5–5 cm) below this point. As a rule of thumb, the Pratt knot will lift the wide end by this distance as you tie the knot.<ref>http://www.realmenrealstyle.com/pratt-shelby-milanese-necktie-knot/</ref>[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 8.jpg|center]]

#*The narrow end of the tie should be higher than the wide end. It will usually be around belly button level, but this is less important than the wide end's placement.<ref>http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/pratt</ref>
#Cross the wide end under the narrow end. Move the wide end across your body to the left side, placing it underneath the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 7.jpg|center]]
#*Do not move the narrow end of the tie for any part of this knot.<ref>http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/pratt</ref> Just hold it steady while you use the wide end.
#Bring the wide end up to the loop around the neck. Place the tip on top of the loop, still on your left side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 7.jpg|center]]

#Pull the wide end through the neck loop. Insert the wide end down into the loop from above. Pull it through in the same direction it lay before, on the left.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 7.jpg|center]]

#Fold the wide end over the narrow end, from left to right. This flips the wide end so the seam is no longer visible. The wide end will extend at an angle off to your right.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 7.jpg|center]]
#Pull the wide end up through the neck loop. Bring the wide end up to your neck loop again, but this time from below. Pull it through.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 7.jpg|center]]

#Tuck the wide end down through the new loop at the front. Your last fold created a horizontal loop at the front of your tie. Tuck the wide end through this loop, and pull straight down to tighten. The wide end should now rest in front of the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 7.jpg|center]]
#Slide the knot to adjust. Pull down on the wide end to tighten. Slide the front knot up to the base of your collar to fasten the tie.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 7.jpg|center]]
#*To create a dimple just below the front knot, squeeze the sides of the knot gently as you tighten.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/pratt/</ref>
=== Half Windsor Knot (Formal)===

#Position the wide end on the right side. Place the tie around your neck and let the sides hang in front of you. The wide end should be on the right side of your body, and hang roughly 12 inches (30 cm) lower than the narrow end on the left.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/halfwindsor/</ref>[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 7.jpg|center]]

#*The Half Windsor is a triangular, symmetrical knot suitable for formal occasions. Larger than the Four-in-hand but less bulky than the Windsor, this can work with most neckties and collar types.<ref>Chic Simple, ''Shirt and Tie'', p. 37, (1993), ISBN 0-500-01593-7</ref> Neckties made from thicker fabric will likely require a spread or wide spread collar with this knot.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>
#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Bring the wide end of the tie over to your left side, crossing over the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 7.jpg|center]]
#Fold the wide end back under the narrow end. Complete a loop around the narrow end and pull the wide end back to the right side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 7.jpg|center]]
#*The underside of the wide end should be visible at this point.
#Take the wide end up to the neck loop. Raise the wide end up to the loop of necktie at your collar. Keep it on the right side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 7.jpg|center]]

#Pull the wide end through the loop and to the left. Insert the wide tip down through the loop and pull it through from the left side, so it crosses under the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 7.jpg|center]]
#Fold the wide end over the front of the narrow end. Bring the wide end back across the front and onto your right side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 7.jpg|center]]
#Slide the wide end up through the neck loop. Fold the wide end up through the neck loop a second time.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 7.jpg|center]]

#Insert the wide end down through the front knot. Loosen the front knot with your finger and insert the wide end. Pull it through to rest over the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 7.jpg|center]]
#Pull on the wide end to tighten. Gently squeeze the front knot as you pull to slide the knot up and create a dimple at the front of your tie.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 7.jpg|center]]
=== Traditional Windsor knot (Extra Formal)===

#Put the tie around your neck. Make sure the wider end is on the right, and about 14 inches (36 cm) lower than the thinner side on the left.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/windsor/</ref> The Windsor knot uses a lot of cloth, so the lower end should start a bit lower than you would usually position a tie.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 7.jpg|center]]

#*Many consider the large, symmetric Windsor knot the most elegant and formal option. Wear it with a spread or wide spread collar.<ref>Thuy Tranthi, ''Tie a Windsor Knot'', in ''The Expert's Guide to 100 Things Everyone Should Know How to Do'', p. 51, (2004), ISBN 1-74114-586-4</ref>

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Hold one end in each hand, then pass each of them to the opposite hand. The wide end should now be on your left side.<ref>http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/windsor</ref><ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/windsor/</ref>[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 7.jpg|center]]

#Bring the wide end up through the neck loop. Using your right hand, hold the two ends where they cross near your collar. With your left hand, pull the wide end up through the neck loop from below.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 7.jpg|center]]
#Bring your tie back down. Rest the wide end back on your chest, to the left of the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 7.jpg|center]]

#Fold it end behind the narrow end. Grab the wide end with your right hand and pull it back to the right side of your body, under the narrow end. Hold the knot near your collar in place with your left hand.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 7.jpg|center]]
#Bring the wide end up to the neck loop from the front. Keep it on the right side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 7.jpg|center]]

#Pull the wide end through the neck loop. Insert the tip of the wide end and pull through, still on the right side. The underside of the wide end should now be facing forward.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 7.jpg|center]]
#Fold the wide end over the narrow end. Fold it back over from right to left, so the front side is visible again.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 7.jpg|center]]
#Pull the wide end through the neck loop from below. Bring the wide end back up through the neck loop one last time.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 7.jpg|center]]
#Insert the wide end through the front knot. Place the wide end through the horizontal knot at the front of the tie. Pull it through.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 8.jpg|center]]

#Tighten the knot. Hold the base of the front knot and squeeze gently from the sides. Slowly pull the wide end of the tie to bring the knot closer to the neck.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 7.jpg|center]]
== Tips ==
*Left-handed people may find it easier to switch the starting positions of the wide and narrow ends. If you do this, switch all "left" and "right" instructions.

*Ideally, the tip of the tie should graze the top of your belt buckle. It's all right if the tie dips down to the bottom of the belt buckle ("Italian style"). If it's any lower, try a knot that uses plenty of cloth (such as the Windsor), or switch to a shorter tie.<ref>http://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052702303491404579391701064546672</ref> Similarly, if the tie ends above your belt, buy a longer tie or try the Pratt knot, which doesn't use much cloth in the knot.
*If your tie has a loop underneath the wide side of the tie, you may slide the narrow side through that loop to prevent it from "peeking" from behind the wide side of the tie.

*To make a dimple, hold the top blade on both edges, then pull it down gently until the top blade starts to tighten. A slightly convex shape should appear close to the knot. Use your thumb and forefinger to press the bottom of the knot into a V-shape and the convex will deepen to form the dimple.
*[[Memorize a List Using Numbers and Rhyming Words|Make a mnemonic device to help you remember]] these steps, such as the word OUAT, which is an acronym for over, under, around and through.

#Cross the wide end under the narrow end. Move the wide end across your body to the left side, placing it underneath the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 6.jpg|center]]
#Bring the wide end up to the loop around the neck. Place the tip on top of the loop, still on your left side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 6.jpg|center]]

#Pull the wide end through the neck loop. Insert the wide end down into the loop from above. Pull it through in the same direction it lay before, on the left.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 6.jpg|center]]

#Fold the wide end over the narrow end, from left to right. This flips the wide end so the seam is no longer visible. The wide end will extend at an angle off to your right.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 6.jpg|center]]
#Pull the wide end up through the neck loop. Bring the wide end up to your neck loop again, but this time from below. Pull it through.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 6.jpg|center]]

#Tuck the wide end down through the new loop at the front. Your last fold created a horizontal loop at the front of your tie. Tuck the wide end through this loop, and pull straight down to tighten. The wide end should now rest in front of the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 6.jpg|center]]
#Slide the knot to adjust. Pull down on the wide end to tighten. Slide the front knot up to the base of your collar to fasten the tie.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 6.jpg|center]]

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Bring the wide end of the tie over to your left side, crossing over the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 6.jpg|center]]

#Pull the wide end through the loop and to the left. Insert the wide tip down through the loop and pull it through from the left side, so it crosses under the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 6.jpg|center]]
#Fold the wide end over the front of the narrow end. Bring the wide end back across the front and onto your right side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 6.jpg|center]]
#Slide the wide end up through the neck loop. Fold the wide end up through the neck loop a second time.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 6.jpg|center]]

#Insert the wide end down through the front knot. Loosen the front knot with your finger and insert the wide end. Pull it through to rest over the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 6.jpg|center]]
#Pull on the wide end to tighten. Gently squeeze the front knot as you pull to slide the knot up and create a dimple at the front of your tie.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 6.jpg|center]]

#Put the tie around your neck. Make sure the wider end is on the right, and about 14 inches (36 cm) lower than the thinner side on the left.<ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/windsor/</ref> The Windsor knot uses a lot of cloth, so the lower end should start a bit lower than you would usually position a tie.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 6.jpg|center]]

#Bring the wide end up to the neck loop from the front. Keep it on the right side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 6.jpg|center]]

#Pull the wide end through the neck loop. Insert the tip of the wide end and pull through, still on the right side. The underside of the wide end should now be facing forward.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 6.jpg|center]]
#Fold the wide end over the narrow end. Fold it back over from right to left, so the front side is visible again.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 6.jpg|center]]
#Pull the wide end through the neck loop from below. Bring the wide end back up through the neck loop one last time.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 6.jpg|center]]
#Insert the wide end through the front knot. Place the wide end through the horizontal knot at the front of the tie. Pull it through.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 6.jpg|center]]

#Tighten the knot. Hold the base of the front knot and squeeze gently from the sides. Slowly pull the wide end of the tie to bring the knot closer to the neck.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 6.jpg|center]]

added: {{fa}}Have you graduated beyond the clip-on tie? Beginning with these helpful instructions, a sharp-looking tie, a mirror, and some patience, you can become an expert in tying your own fashionable knot. You have several options available, from the versatile Four-in-Hand Knot to the classic Windsor.

#Drape the tie around your neck. With your collar up and your shirt fully buttoned, place the tie around your shoulders. Hang the wider end of the tie on your right side, with the narrow end about 12 inches (30 cm) higher on the left.<ref>https://www.thetiebar.com/how-to-tie/four-in-hand</ref>
#*Avoid spread collars with this small, asymmetric knot.<ref>http://www.necktieadvisor.com/men%E2%80%99s-tie-knots-and-when-to-use-them/</ref>
#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Bring the wide end to the left side of your body, over the narrow end. Hold the two pieces of cloth together with your left hand, near your neck.
#Loop the wide end under the narrow end. Let go with your right hand. Tuck it underneath the narrow end, grab the wide end, and pull it back through to your right side.

#Loop the wide end back over again. Cross it over the narrow end one more time, at the same point where your left hand is holding the knot together. The front of the tie should be facing forward again (so the seam is hidden).
#Pull the wide end up through the neck loop. Fold the tip of the wide end under itself and pull up through the neck loop.<ref>https://www.thetiebar.com/how-to-tie/four-in-hand</ref>
#Insert the wide end down through the front knot. You should have a horizontal knot across the front of your tie. Hold this knot open with your finger and carefully insert the wide end.
#Tighten the knot. Hold the narrow end and slide the front knot up to tighten the tie. Make sure your tie is straight and the length is appropriate, ideally ending at the top of your belt buckle.

=== Half Windsor Knot (Formal)===
#Slide the wide end up through the neck loop. Fold the wide end up through the neck loop a second time.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 16.jpg|center]]
=== Traditional Windsor knot (Extra Formal)===

#*Many consider the large, symmetric Windsor knot the most elegant and formal option. Wear it with a spread or wide spread collar.<ref>Thuy Tranthi, ''Tie a Windsor Knot'', in ''The Expert's Guide to 100 Things Everyone Should Know How to Do'', p. 51, (2004), ISBN 1-74114-586-4</ref>

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. Hold one end in each hand, then pass each of them to the opposite hand. The wide end should now be on your left side.<ref>http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/windsor</ref><ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/windsor/</ref>[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 22.jpg|center]]

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end. The wide end should now be on your left side.<ref>http://www.ties.com/how-to-tie-a-tie/windsor</ref><ref>http://www.tie-a-tie.net/windsor/</ref>[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 22.jpg|center]]
#Bring the wide end up through the neck loop. Pull the wide end up through the neck loop from below.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 23.jpg|center]]
#Bring your tie back down. Rest the wide end back on your chest, to the left of the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 24.jpg|center]]
#Fold it behind the narrow end. Bring the wide end under the narrow end, to the right side of your body.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 25.jpg|center]]
#Bring the wide end up to the neck loop from the front. Keep it on the right side.

#Pull the wide end through the neck loop. Insert the tip of the wide end and pull through, still on the right side. The underside of the wide end should now be facing forward.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 26.jpg|center]]
#Fold the wide end over the narrow end. Fold it back over from right to left, so the front side is visible again.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 27.jpg|center]]
#Pull the wide end through the neck loop from below. Bring the wide end back up through the neck loop one last time.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 28.jpg|center]]
#Insert the wide end through the front knot. Place the wide end through the horizontal knot at the front of the tie. Pull it through.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 29.jpg|center]]
#Tighten the knot. Hold the base of the front knot and squeeze gently from the sides. Slowly pull the narrow end of the tie to bring the knot closer to the neck.[[Image:4831 30.jpg|center]]
*Left-handed people may find it easier to switch the starting positions of the wide and narrow ends. If you do this, switch all "left" and "right" instructions.

*Ideally, the tip of the tie should graze the top of your belt buckle. It's all right if the tie dips down to the bottom of the belt buckle ("Italian style"). If it's any lower, try a knot that uses plenty of cloth (such as the Windsor), or switch to a shorter tie.<ref>http://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052702303491404579391701064546672</ref> Similarly, if the tie ends above your belt, buy a longer tie or try the Pratt knot, which doesn't use much cloth in the knot.
*If your tie has a loop underneath the wide side of the tie, you may slide the narrow side through that loop to prevent it from "peeking" from behind the wide side of the tie.

*To make a dimple, hold the top blade on both edges, then pull it down gently until the top blade starts to tighten. A slightly convex shape should appear close to the knot. Use your thumb and forefinger to press the bottom of the knot into a V-shape and the convex will deepen to form the dimple.
*[[Memorize a List Using Numbers and Rhyming Words|Make a mnemonic device to help you remember]] these steps, such as the word OUAT, which is an acronym for over, under, around and through.

#*Many men with shorter necks prefer the four-in-hand, because the knot at top is very narrow and has a slimming effect on the rest of the neck.

# Slide the wide side up through the loop around your neck.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 16.jpg|center]]

#  Put the tie around your neck. One end should be considerably wider than the other. Make sure the wider end is on the right, and about a foot (30cm) lower than the thinner side on the left.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 21.jpg|center]]
#  Cross the wide end over the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 22.jpg|center]]
# Bring your tie up through the loop.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 23.jpg|center]]
#Bring your tie back down. The wide end should be resting to the left of the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 24.jpg|center]]
# Pull the wide end underneath the narrow end and to the right! [[Image:Tie a Tie Step 25.jpg|center]]
#Pull the wide end through the loop, this time on the right side. The wide end should now be inside out.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 26.jpg|center]]
#  Cross the wide end over the thin end again, from right to left.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 27.jpg|center]]
#  Bring the wide end under the loop.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 28.jpg|center]]
#Fold the wide end through the loop and into the knot at the front of the tie.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 29.jpg|center]]
#  Tighten the knot into a triangle using both hands. Slowly tighten the  narrow end to bring the tie closer to the neck.[[Image:4831 30.jpg|center]]

#*For a more modern, fashionable and casual look, make the knot a good few inches or centimeters down below the collar. For all formal occasions, however, keep the knot at the traditional distance away from the collar.
* Look in a mirror while doing this.
*Try exploring with different sizes to get the hang of it.
*There are different types of knots you can tie, some of which are more appropriate to formal occasions (like the Windsor knot), while others are casual.
*In general, the wide end of the tie should hang twice as low as the narrow end.

*To make a dimple, hold the top blade on both edges and then pull it down gently until the top blade starts to tighten. A slight convex should appear close to the knot. Use your thumb and forefinger to press the bottom of the knot into a V-shape and the convex will deepen to form the dimple.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 8.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 5-preview Version 8.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 6.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 8.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 8.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end up through the loop.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 8.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 6-preview Version 8.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 6.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 8.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 8.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end down all the way through the knot in the front.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 8.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 7-preview Version 8.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 6.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 8.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 8.360p.first.gif}}

#Shape the knot into a triangle shape and pull on the narrow end to fasten the tie along the collar.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 8.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 8-preview Version 8.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 6.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 8.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 8.360p.first.gif}}

#Stand in front of the [[Make a Mirror|mirror]]. Your collar should be up, your shirt buttoned all the way to the top, and the tie around your neck. The wide end of the tie should be on the side of your [[Determine Your Dominant Hand|dominant hand]]. So if you're right-handed, the wider end should be hanging on your right side. If you're left-handed,the wider end should be hanging on your left side.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 8.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 9-preview Version 8.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 6.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 8.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 8.360p.first.gif}}

#Look for a [[Mend a Torn Seam|seam]] on the front of the narrow end of the tie.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 8.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 10-preview Version 7.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 8.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 8.360p.first.gif}}

#Move the wide end over the narrow end so they cross each other on the seam.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 8.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 11-preview Version 7.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 8.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 8.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end behind the narrow end.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 8.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 12-preview Version 7.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 8.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 8.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end around. It should be facing off to your left.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 8.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 13-preview Version 7.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 8.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 8.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end under the narrow end again.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 8.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 14-preview Version 7.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 8.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 8.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end of the tie under the loop around your neck.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 8.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 15-preview Version 7.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 8.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 8.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end down ''through'' the knot at the front of the tie.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 8.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 16-preview Version 7.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 8.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 8.360p.first.gif}}

#Tighten the knot by sliding it up the narrow end. Make sure your tie is straight and the length is appropriate.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 7.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 17-preview Version 6.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 7.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 7.360p.first.gif}}

#Choose the Half Windsor as an alternative to the Four-in-Hand method of tying a tie. {{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 6.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 18-preview Version 5.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 6.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 6.360p.first.gif}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 7.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 20-preview Version 6.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 7.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 7.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide side around and under the narrow side.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 7.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 21-preview Version 6.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 7.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 7.360p.first.gif}}

#Take the wide side over the loop around the neck. Tighten a bit.

#Bring the wide side over the narrow side, out front, moving from right to left.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 7.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 23-preview Version 6.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 7.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 7.360p.first.gif}}

#Slide the wide side up through the loop around your neck.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 7.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 24-preview Version 6.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 7.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 7.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide side through the knot in the front.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 7.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 25-preview Version 6.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 7.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 7.360p.first.gif}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 7.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 26-preview Version 6.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 7.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 7.360p.first.gif}}

#Tighten the tie around your [[Fit a Martingale Collar|collar]] by pulling on the narrow side of the tie (which should now be hidden underneath the wide side of the tie). {{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 7.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 27-preview Version 6.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 7.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 7.360p.first.gif}}

#Choose the traditional Windsor knot as a more formal alternative to the Half Windsor. The Duke of Windsor started the trend for this knot back in the 1930s. #Pull the wide end underneath the narrow end and to the right!

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 6.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 33-preview Version 6.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 6.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 6.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end through the loop, this time on the right side. The wide end should now be inside out.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 6.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 34-preview Version 6.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 6.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 6.360p.first.gif}}

#Cross the wide end over the thin end again, from right to left.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 6.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 35-preview Version 6.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 6.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 6.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end under the loop.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 6.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 36-preview Version 6.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 6.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 6.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end through the loop and into the knot at the front of the tie.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 37 Version 6.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 37-preview Version 6.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 37 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 37 Version 6.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 37 Version 6.360p.first.gif}}

#Tighten the knot into a triangle using both hands. Slowly tighten the  narrow end to bring the tie closer to the neck.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 38 Version 6.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 38-preview Version 6.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 38 Version 5.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 38 Version 6.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 38 Version 6.360p.first.gif}}

# Place the tie around your neck with the wide side on the right side of your body. Adjust the tie so that the length of the wide side is about three times the length of the narrow side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 11.jpg|center]]

# Bring the wide side through the knot in the front.  [[Image:Tie a Tie Step 17.jpg|center]]
#Tighten a bit and shape the knot into a triangle shape. You want your knot to look a bit wider than the Four-in-Hand knot.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 18.jpg|center]]

# Tighten the tie around your [[Fit a Martingale Collar|collar]] by pulling on the narrow side of the tie (which should now be hidden underneath the wide side of the tie). If your tie has a loop underneath the wide side of the tie, you may slide the narrow side through that loop to prevent it from "peeking" from behind the wide side of the tie.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 19.jpg|center]]

# Choose the traditional Windsor knot as a more formal alternative to the Half Windsor. The Duke of Windsor started the trend for this knot back in the 1930s. It's more dignified than the Four-in-Hand knot, but a little harder to tie. # Choose the traditional Windsor knot as a more formal alternative to the Half Windsor. The Duke of Windsor started the trend for this knot back in the 1930s. It has remained popular to this day because it projects a statement that suggests the wearer is elegant and has [[Be Confident|confidence]]. It's more dignified than the Four-in-Hand knot, but a little harder to tie. This knot should be worn with a spread collar.<ref>Thuy Tranthi, ''Tie a Windsor Knot'', in ''The Expert's Guide to 100 Things Everyone Should Know How to Do'', p. 51, (2004), ISBN 1-74114-586-4</ref>[[Image:4831 20.jpg|center]]

#  Put the tie around your neck. One end should be considerably wider than the other. Make sure the wider end is on the right, and about a foot (30cm) lower than the thinner side on the left.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 21.jpg|center]]
#  Cross the wide end over the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 22.jpg|center]]
# Bring your tie up through the loop.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 23.jpg|center]]
#Bring your tie back down. The wide end should be resting to the left of the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 24.jpg|center]]
# Pull the wide end underneath the narrow end and to the right! [[Image:Tie a Tie Step 25.jpg|center]]
#Pull the wide end through the loop, this time on the right side. The wide end should now be inside out.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 26.jpg|center]]
#  Cross the wide end over the thin end again, from right to left.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 27.jpg|center]]
#  Bring the wide end under the loop.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 28.jpg|center]]
#Fold the wide end through the loop and into the knot at the front of the tie.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 29.jpg|center]]
#  Tighten the knot into a triangle using both hands. Slowly tighten the  narrow end to bring the tie closer to the neck.[[Image:4831 30.jpg|center]]

added:
#Start with the tie inside out. The wide end of the tie should be hanging on the right, and the narrow end on the left. Adjust the tie so that the wider end is a few cms lengthier than the narrow end.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 1 Version 6.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 1-preview Version 5.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 1 Version 4.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 1 Version 6.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 1 Version 6.360p.first.gif}}

#Cross the wide end under the narrow end.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 6.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 2-preview Version 5.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 4.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 6.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 6.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end over the loop around the neck.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 6.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 3-preview Version 5.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 4.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 6.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 6.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end under to complete the loop around the neck. Tighten.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 5.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 4-preview Version 5.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 4.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 5.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 5.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end over the narrow end, from left to right.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 5.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 5-preview Version 5.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 4.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 5.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 5.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end up through the loop.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 5.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 6-preview Version 5.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 4.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 5.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 5.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end down all the way through the knot in the front.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 5.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 7-preview Version 5.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 4.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 5.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 5.360p.first.gif}}

#Shape the knot into a triangle shape and pull on the narrow end to fasten the tie along the collar.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 5.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 8-preview Version 5.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 4.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 5.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 5.360p.first.gif}}

#Stand in front of the [[Make a Mirror|mirror]]. Your collar should be up, your shirt buttoned all the way to the top, and the tie around your neck. The wide end of the tie should be on the side of your [[Determine Your Dominant Hand|dominant hand]]. So if you're right-handed, the wider end should be hanging on your right side. If you're left-handed,the wider end should be hanging on your left side.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 5.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 9-preview Version 5.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 4.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 5.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 5.360p.first.gif}}

#Look for a [[Mend a Torn Seam|seam]] on the front of the narrow end of the tie.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 5.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 10-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 5.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 5.360p.first.gif}}

#Move the wide end over the narrow end so they cross each other on the seam.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 5.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 11-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 5.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 5.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end behind the narrow end.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 5.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 12-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 5.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 5.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end around. It should be facing off to your left.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 5.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 13-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 5.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 5.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end under the narrow end again.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 5.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 14-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 5.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 5.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end of the tie under the loop around your neck.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 5.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 15-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 5.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 5.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end down ''through'' the knot at the front of the tie.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 5.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 16-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 5.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 5.360p.first.gif}}

#Tighten the knot by sliding it up the narrow end. Make sure your tie is straight and the length is appropriate.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 17-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

#Choose the Half Windsor as an alternative to the Four-in-Hand method of tying a tie. The knot is bigger, resembles a triangle, and is considered to be more distinguished than the four-in-hand (but not as distinguished as the full Windsor). Most men tend to prefer the half Windsor because it isn't as bulky to wear.Chic Simple, ''Shirt and Tie'', p. 37, (1993), ISBN 0-500-01593-7

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 18-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

#Place the tie around your neck with the wide side on the right side of your body. Adjust the tie so that the length of the wide side is about three times the length of the narrow side.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 19-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

#Cross the wide side of the [[Tie a Tie|tie]] over the narrow side.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 20-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide side around and under the narrow side.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 21-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

#Take the wide side over the loop around the neck. Tighten a bit.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 22-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide side over the narrow side, out front, moving from right to left.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 23-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

#Slide the wide side up through the loop around your neck.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 24-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide side through the knot in the front.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 25-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

#Tighten a bit and shape the knot into a triangle shape. You want your knot to look a bit wider than the Four-in-Hand knot.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 26-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

#Tighten the tie around your [[Fit a Martingale Collar|collar]] by pulling on the narrow side of the tie (which should now be hidden underneath the wide side of the tie). If your tie has a loop underneath the wide side of the tie, you may slide the narrow side through that loop to prevent it from "peeking" from behind the wide side of the tie.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 27-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

#Choose the traditional Windsor knot as a more formal alternative to the Half Windsor. The Duke of Windsor started the trend for this knot back in the 1930s. It has remained popular to this day because it projects a statement that suggests the wearer is elegant and has [[Be Confident|confidence]]. It's more dignified than the Four-in-Hand knot, but a little harder to tie. This knot should be worn with a spread collar.Thuy Tranthi, ''Tie a Windsor Knot'', in ''The Expert's Guide to 100 Things Everyone Should Know How to Do'', p. 51, (2004), ISBN 1-74114-586-4

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 28-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

#Put the tie around your neck. One end should be considerably wider than the other. Make sure the wider end is on the right, and about a foot (30cm) lower than the thinner side on the left.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 29-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 30-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring your tie up through the loop.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 31-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 3.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 3.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring your tie back down. The wide end should be resting to the left of the narrow end.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 32-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 3.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 3.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end underneath the narrow end and to the right!

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 33-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 3.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 3.360p.first.gif}}

#Pull the wide end through the loop, this time on the right side. The wide end should now be inside out.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 34-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 3.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 3.360p.first.gif}}

#Cross the wide end over the thin end again, from right to left.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 35-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 3.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 3.360p.first.gif}}

#Bring the wide end under the loop.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 36-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 3.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 3.360p.first.gif}}

#Fold the wide end through the loop and into the knot at the front of the tie.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 37 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 37-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 37 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 37 Version 3.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 37 Version 3.360p.first.gif}}

#Tighten the knot into a triangle using both hands. Slowly tighten the  narrow end to bring the tie closer to the neck.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 38 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 38-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 38 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 38 Version 3.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 38 Version 3.360p.first.gif}}

added: {{fa}}Have you ever tried to tie a tie, only to end up with a horrible tangled knot? Beginning with these helpful instructions, a sharp-looking tie, a mirror and some patience, you can become an expert in tying a fabulous tie. Because there are several different ways to tie a tie, this article listed a few several methods, starting with the easiest tie to tie.
# Bring the wide end over the loop around the neck. [[Image:Tie a Tie Step 33.jpg|center]]

=== Half Windsor Knot ===

# Choose the Half Windsor as an alternative to the Four-in-Hand method of tying a tie. The knot is bigger, resembles a triangle, and is considered to be more distinguished than the four-in-hand (but not as distinguished as the full Windsor). Most men tend to prefer the half Windsor because it isn't as bulky to wear.<ref>Chic Simple, ''Shirt and Tie'', p. 37, (1993), ISBN 0-500-01593-7</ref>[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 10.jpg|center]]

# Place the tie around your neck with the wide side on the right side of your body. Adjust the tie so that the length of the wide side is about three times the length of the narrow side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 11.jpg|center]]
#*You may need to experiment with this step to achieve the right length for the sides of the ties. Some people prefer having the wide side about 12 inches (30 centimeters) below the narrow side.
# Cross the wide side of the [[Tie a Tie|tie]] over the narrow side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 12.jpg|center]]
#Bring the wide side around and under the narrow side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 13.jpg|center]]
# Take the wide side over the loop around the neck. Tighten a bit. [[Image:Tie a Tie Step 14.jpg|center]]
# Bring the wide side over the narrow side, out front, moving from right to left.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 15.jpg|center]]
# Slide the wide side up through the loop around your neck.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 16.jpg|center]]
# Bring the wide side through the knot in the front.  [[Image:Tie a Tie Step 17.jpg|center]]
#Tighten a bit and shape the knot into a triangle shape. You want your knot to look a bit wider than the Four-in-Hand knot.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 18.jpg|center]]

# Tighten the tie around your [[Fit a Martingale Collar|collar]] by pulling on the narrow side of the tie (which should now be hidden underneath the wide side of the tie). If your tie has a loop underneath the wide side of the tie, you may slide the narrow side through that loop to prevent it from "peeking" from behind the wide side of the tie.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 19.jpg|center]]
=== Traditional Windsor knot ===

# Choose the traditional Windsor knot as a more formal alternative to the Half Windsor. The Duke of Windsor started the trend for this knot back in the 1930s. It has remained popular to this day because it projects a statement that suggests the wearer is elegant and has [[Be Confident|confidence]]. It's more dignified than the Four-in-Hand knot, but a little harder to tie. This knot should be worn with a spread collar.<ref>Thuy Tranthi, ''Tie a Windsor Knot'', in ''The Expert's Guide to 100 Things Everyone Should Know How to Do'', p. 51, (2004), ISBN 1-74114-586-4</ref>[[Image:4831 20.jpg|center]]

#  Put the tie around your neck. One end should be considerably wider than the other. Make sure the wider end is on the right, and about a foot (30cm) lower than the thinner side on the left.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 21.jpg|center]]
#  Cross the wide end over the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 22.jpg|center]]
# Bring your tie up through the loop.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 23.jpg|center]]
#Bring your tie back down. The wide end should be resting to the left of the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 24.jpg|center]]
# Pull the wide end underneath the narrow end and to the right! [[Image:Tie a Tie Step 25.jpg|center]]
#Pull the wide end through the loop, this time on the right side. The wide end should now be inside out.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 26.jpg|center]]
#  Cross the wide end over the thin end again, from right to left.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 27.jpg|center]]
#  Bring the wide end under the loop.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 28.jpg|center]]
#Fold the wide end through the loop and into the knot at the front of the tie.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 29.jpg|center]]
#  Tighten the knot into a triangle using both hands. Slowly tighten the  narrow end to bring the tie closer to the neck.[[Image:4831 30.jpg|center]]

#*For a more modern, fashionable and casual look, make the knot a good few inches or centimeters down below the collar. For all formal occasions, however, keep the knot at the traditional distance away from the collar.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 4-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 8-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 9-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 3.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 4.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 4.360p.first.gif}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 7-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 3.jpg}}

#Cross the wide end over the thin end again, from right to left.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 8-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 3.jpg}}

#Bring the wide end under the loop.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 9-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 3.jpg}}

#Fold the wide end through the loop and into the knot at the front of the tie.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 10-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 2.jpg}}

#Tighten the knot into a triangle using both hands. Slowly tighten the  narrow end to bring the tie closer to the neck.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 11-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 2.jpg}}

#*For a more modern, fashionable and casual look, make the knot a good few inches or centimeters down below the collar. For all formal occasions, however, keep the knot at the traditional distance away from the collar.
=== Half Windsor Knot ===

#Choose the Half Windsor as an alternative to the Four-in-Hand method of tying a tie. The knot is bigger, resembles a triangle, and is considered to be more distinguished than the four-in-hand (but not as distinguished as the full Windsor). Most men tend to prefer the half Windsor because it isn't as bulky to wear.Chic Simple, ''Shirt and Tie'', p. 37, (1993), ISBN 0-500-01593-7

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 12-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 2.jpg}}

#Place the tie around your neck with the wide side on the right side of your body. Adjust the tie so that the length of the wide side is about three times the length of the narrow side.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 13-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 2.jpg}}
#*You may need to experiment with this step to achieve the right length for the sides of the ties. Some people prefer having the wide side about 12 inches (30 centimeters) below the narrow side.

#Cross the wide side of the [[Tie a Tie|tie]] over the narrow side.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 14-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bring the wide side around and under the narrow side.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 15-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 2.jpg}}

#Take the wide side over the loop around the neck. Tighten a bit.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 16-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bring the wide side over the narrow side, out front, moving from right to left.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 17-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 2.jpg}}

#Slide the wide side up through the loop around your neck.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 18-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bring the wide side through the knot in the front.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 19-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 2.jpg}}

#Tighten a bit and shape the knot into a triangle shape. You want your knot to look a bit wider than the Four-in-Hand knot.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 20-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 2.jpg}}

#Tighten the tie around your [[Fit a Martingale Collar|collar]] by pulling on the narrow side of the tie (which should now be hidden underneath the wide side of the tie). If your tie has a loop underneath the wide side of the tie, you may slide the narrow side through that loop to prevent it from "peeking" from behind the wide side of the tie.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 21-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 2.jpg}}

#Start with the tie inside out. The wide end of the tie should be hanging on the right, and the narrow end on the left. Adjust the tie so that the wider end is a few cms lengthier than the narrow end.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 22-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 2.jpg}}

#Cross the wide end under the narrow end.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 23-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bring the wide end over the loop around the neck.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 24-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 2.jpg}}

#Pull the wide end under to complete the loop around the neck. Tighten.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 25-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bring the wide end over the narrow end, from left to right.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 26-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 2.jpg}}

#Pull the wide end up through the loop.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 27-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bring the wide end down all the way through the knot in the front.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 28-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 2.jpg}}

#Shape the knot into a triangle shape and pull on the narrow end to fasten the tie along the collar.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 29-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 2.jpg}}

#Stand in front of the [[Make a Mirror|mirror]]. Your collar should be up, your shirt buttoned all the way to the top, and the tie around your neck. The wide end of the tie should be on the side of your [[Determine Your Dominant Hand|dominant hand]]. So if you're right-handed, the wider end should be hanging on your right side. If you're left-handed,the wider end should be hanging on your left side.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 30-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 2.jpg}}

#Look for a [[Mend a Torn Seam|seam]] on the front of the narrow end of the tie.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 31-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 2.jpg}}

#Move the wide end over the narrow end so they cross each other on the seam.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 32-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 2.jpg}}

#Pull the wide end behind the narrow end.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 33-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bring the wide end around. It should be facing off to your left.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 34-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bring the wide end under the narrow end again.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 35-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 2.jpg}}

#Pull the wide end of the tie under the loop around your neck.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 36-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 2.jpg}}

#Pull the wide end down ''through'' the knot at the front of the tie.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 37 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 37-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 37 Version 2.jpg}}

#Tighten the knot by sliding it up the narrow end. Make sure your tie is straight and the length is appropriate.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 38 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 38-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 38 Version 2.jpg}}

=== Half Windsor Knot ===

# Choose the Half Windsor as an alternative to the Four-in-Hand method of tying a tie. The knot is bigger, resembles a triangle, and is considered to be more distinguished than the four-in-hand (but not as distinguished as the full Windsor). Most men tend to prefer the half Windsor because it isn't as bulky to wear.<ref>Chic Simple, ''Shirt and Tie'', p. 37, (1993), ISBN 0-500-01593-7</ref>[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 10.jpg|center]]

# Place the tie around your neck with the wide side on the right side of your body. Adjust the tie so that the length of the wide side is about three times the length of the narrow side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 11.jpg|center]]
#*You may need to experiment with this step to achieve the right length for the sides of the ties. Some people prefer having the wide side about 12 inches (30 centimeters) below the narrow side.

#Bring the wide side around and under the narrow side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 13.jpg|center]]

# Bring the wide side over the narrow side, out front, moving from right to left.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 15.jpg|center]]
# Slide the wide side up through the loop around your neck.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 16.jpg|center]]
# Bring the wide side through the knot in the front.  [[Image:Tie a Tie Step 17.jpg|center]]

# Choose the traditional Windsor knot as a more formal alternative to the Half Windsor. The Duke of Windsor started the trend for this knot back in the 1930s. It's more dignified than the Four-in-Hand knot, but a little harder to tie. #  Bring the wide end under the loop.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 28.jpg|center]]

#Pull the wide end through the loop, this time on the right side. The wide end should now be inside out.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 26.jpg|center]]
#  Cross the wide end over the thin end again, from right to left.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 27.jpg|center]]
#  Bring the wide end under the loop.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 28.jpg|center]]
#Fold the wide end through the loop and into the knot at the front of the tie.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 29.jpg|center]]
#  Tighten the knot into a triangle using both hands. Slowly tighten the  narrow end to bring the tie closer to the neck.[[Image:4831 30.jpg|center]]

# Choose the Half Windsor as an alternative to the Four-in-Hand method of tying a tie. The knot is bigger, resembles a triangle, and is considered to be more distinguished than the four-in-hand (but not as distinguished as the full Windsor). Most men tend to prefer the half Windsor because it isn't as bulky to wear.<ref>Chic Simple, ''Shirt and Tie'', p. 37, (1993), ISBN 0-500-01593-7</ref>[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 10.jpg|center]]

# Cross the wide side of the [[Tie a Tie|tie]] over the narrow side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 12.jpg|center]]
#Bring the wide side around and under the narrow side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 13.jpg|center]]

# Slide the wide side up through the loop around your neck.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 16.jpg|center]]
# Bring the wide side through the knot in the front.  [[Image:Tie a Tie Step 17.jpg|center]]

If your tie has a loop underneath the wide side of the tie, you may slide the narrow side through that loop to prevent it from "peeking" from behind the wide side of the tie.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 19.jpg|center]]

removed: # Choose the traditional Windsor knot as a more formal alternative to the Half Windsor. The Duke of Windsor started the trend for this knot back in the 1930s. It has remained popular to this day because it projects a statement that suggests the wearer is elegant and has [[Be Confident|confidence]]. It's more dignified than the Four-in-Hand knot, but a little harder to tie. This knot should be worn with a spread collar.<ref>Thuy Tranthi, ''Tie a Windsor Knot'', in ''The Expert's Guide to 100 Things Everyone Should Know How to Do'', p. 51, (2004), ISBN 1-74114-586-4</ref>[[Image:4831 20.jpg|center]]

#  Put the tie around your neck. One end should be considerably wider than the other. Make sure the wider end is on the right, and about a foot (30cm) lower than the thinner side on the left.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 21.jpg|center]]
#  Cross the wide end over the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 22.jpg|center]]
# Bring your tie up through the loop.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 23.jpg|center]]
#Bring your tie back down. The wide end should be resting to the left of the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 24.jpg|center]]
# Pull the wide end underneath the narrow end and to the right! [[Image:Tie a Tie Step 25.jpg|center]]
#Pull the wide end through the loop, this time on the right side. The wide end should now be inside out.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 26.jpg|center]]
#  Cross the wide end over the thin end again, from right to left.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 27.jpg|center]]
#  Bring the wide end under the loop.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 28.jpg|center]]
#Fold the wide end through the loop and into the knot at the front of the tie.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 29.jpg|center]]
#  Tighten the knot into a triangle using both hands. Slowly tighten the  narrow end to bring the tie closer to the neck.[[Image:4831 30.jpg|center]]

# Choose the Half Windsor as an alternative to the Four-in-Hand method of tying a tie. The knot is bigger, resembles a triangle, and is considered to be more distinguished than the four-in-hand (but not as distinguished as the full Windsor). Most men tend to prefer the half Windsor because it isn't as bulky to wear.<ref>Chic Simple, ''Shirt and Tie'', p. 37, (1993), ISBN 0-500-01593-7</ref>[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 10.jpg|center]]

# Place the tie around your neck with the wide side on the right side of your body. Adjust the tie so that the length of the wide side is about three times the length of the narrow side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 11.jpg|center]]
# Cross the wide side of the [[Tie a Tie|tie]] over the narrow side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 12.jpg|center]]
#Bring the wide side around and under the narrow side.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 13.jpg|center]]
# Take the wide side over the loop around the neck. Tighten a bit. [[Image:Tie a Tie Step 14.jpg|center]]
# Bring the wide side over the narrow side, out front, moving from right to left.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 15.jpg|center]]
# Slide the wide side up through the loop around your neck.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 16.jpg|center]]
# Bring the wide side through the knot in the front.  [[Image:Tie a Tie Step 17.jpg|center]]
#Tighten a bit and shape the knot into a triangle shape. You want your knot to look a bit wider than the Four-in-Hand knot.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 18.jpg|center]]

# Tighten the tie around your [[Fit a Martingale Collar|collar]] by pulling on the narrow side of the tie (which should now be hidden underneath the wide side of the tie). If your tie has a loop underneath the wide side of the tie, you may slide the narrow side through that loop to prevent it from "peeking" from behind the wide side of the tie.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 19.jpg|center]]

# Start with the tie inside out. The wide end of the tie should be hanging on the right, and the narrow end on the left. Adjust the tie so that the wider end is a few cms lengthier than the narrow end. [[Image:Tie a Tie Step 31.jpg|center]]
#Cross the wide end under the narrow end.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 32.jpg|center]]
# Bring the wide end over the loop around the neck. [[Image:Tie a Tie Step 33.jpg|center]]
#Pull the wide end under to complete the loop around the neck. Tighten.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 34.jpg|center]]
#Bring the wide end over the narrow end, from left to right.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 35.jpg|center]]
#Pull the wide end up through the loop.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 36.jpg|center]]
#Bring the wide end down all the way through the knot in the front.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 37.jpg|center]]
#Shape the knot into a triangle shape and pull on the narrow end to fasten the tie along the collar.[[Image:Tie a Tie Step 38.jpg|center]]

#Stand in front of the [[Make a Mirror|mirror]]. Your collar should be up, your shirt buttoned all the way to the top, and the tie around your neck. The wide end of the tie should be on the side of your [[Determine Your Dominant Hand|dominant hand]]. So if you're right-handed, the wider end should be hanging on your right side. If you're left-handed,the wider end should be hanging on your left side.

#Bring the wide end under the narrow end again.

#Pull the wide end of the tie under the loop around your neck.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 7-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 2.jpg|gif=Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 3.360p.gif|giffirst=Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 3.360p.first.gif}}

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 2-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 2 Version 3.jpg}}

#Cross the wide end over the narrow end.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 3-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 3 Version 3.jpg}}

#Bring your tie up through the loop.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 4-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 4 Version 3.jpg}}

#Bring your tie back down. The wide end should be resting to the left of the narrow end.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 5-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 5 Version 3.jpg}}

#Pull the wide end underneath the narrow end and to the right!

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 6-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 6 Version 3.jpg}}

#Pull the wide end through the loop, this time on the right side. The wide end should now be inside out.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 7-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 7 Version 3.jpg}}

#Cross the wide end over the thin end again, from right to left.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 8-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 8 Version 3.jpg}}

#Bring the wide end under the loop.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 4.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 9-preview Version 4.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 9 Version 3.jpg}}

#Fold the wide end through the loop and into the knot at the front of the tie.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 10-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 10 Version 2.jpg}}

#Tighten the knot into a triangle using both hands. Slowly tighten the  narrow end to bring the tie closer to the neck.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 11-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 11 Version 2.jpg}}

#Choose the Half Windsor as an alternative to the Four-in-Hand method of tying a tie. The knot is bigger, resembles a triangle, and is considered to be more distinguished than the four-in-hand (but not as distinguished as the full Windsor). Most men tend to prefer the half Windsor because it isn't as bulky to wear.Chic Simple, ''Shirt and Tie'', p. 37, (1993), ISBN 0-500-01593-7

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 12-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 12 Version 2.jpg}}

#Place the tie around your neck with the wide side on the right side of your body. Adjust the tie so that the length of the wide side is about three times the length of the narrow side.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 13-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 13 Version 2.jpg}}

#Cross the wide side of the [[Tie a Tie|tie]] over the narrow side.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 14-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 14 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bring the wide side around and under the narrow side.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 15-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 15 Version 2.jpg}}

#Take the wide side over the loop around the neck. Tighten a bit.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 3.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 16-preview Version 3.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 16 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bring the wide side over the narrow side, out front, moving from right to left.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 17-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 17 Version 2.jpg}}

#Slide the wide side up through the loop around your neck.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 18-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 18 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bring the wide side through the knot in the front.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 19-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 19 Version 2.jpg}}

#Tighten a bit and shape the knot into a triangle shape. You want your knot to look a bit wider than the Four-in-Hand knot.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 20-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 20 Version 2.jpg}}

#Tighten the tie around your [[Fit a Martingale Collar|collar]] by pulling on the narrow side of the tie (which should now be hidden underneath the wide side of the tie). If your tie has a loop underneath the wide side of the tie, you may slide the narrow side through that loop to prevent it from "peeking" from behind the wide side of the tie.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 21-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 21 Version 2.jpg}}

#Start with the tie inside out. The wide end of the tie should be hanging on the right, and the narrow end on the left. Adjust the tie so that the wider end is a few cms lengthier than the narrow end.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 22-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 22 Version 2.jpg}}

#Cross the wide end under the narrow end.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 23-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 23 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bring the wide end over the loop around the neck.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 24-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 24 Version 2.jpg}}

#Pull the wide end under to complete the loop around the neck. Tighten.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 25-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 25 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bring the wide end over the narrow end, from left to right.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 26-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 26 Version 2.jpg}}

#Pull the wide end up through the loop.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 27-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 27 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bring the wide end down all the way through the knot in the front.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 28-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 28 Version 2.jpg}}

#Shape the knot into a triangle shape and pull on the narrow end to fasten the tie along the collar.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 29-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 29 Version 2.jpg}}

#Stand in front of the [[Make a Mirror|mirror]]. Your collar should be up, your shirt buttoned all the way to the top, and the tie around your neck. The wide end of the tie should be on the side of your [[Determine Your Dominant Hand|dominant hand]]. So if you're right-handed, the wider end should be hanging on your right side. If you're left-handed,the wider end should be hanging on your left side.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 30-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 30 Version 2.jpg}}

#Look for a [[Mend a Torn Seam|seam]] on the front of the narrow end of the tie.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 31-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 31 Version 2.jpg}}

#Move the wide end over the narrow end so they cross each other on the seam.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 32-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 32 Version 2.jpg}}

#Pull the wide end behind the narrow end.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 33-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 33 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bring the wide end around. It should be facing off to your left.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 34-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 34 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bring the wide end under the narrow end again.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 35-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 35 Version 2.jpg}}

#Pull the wide end of the tie under the loop around your neck.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 36-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 36 Version 2.jpg}}

#Pull the wide end down ''through'' the knot at the front of the tie.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 37 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 37-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 37 Version 2.jpg}}

#Tighten the knot by sliding it up the narrow end. Make sure your tie is straight and the length is appropriate.

{{whvid|Tie a Tie Step 38 Version 2.360p.mp4|Tie a Tie Step 38-preview Version 2.jpg|Tie a Tie Step 38 Version 2.jpg}}
